story.title: Franco Baresi, AC Milan and Italy Football Legend, Passes Away at 66
story.summary: Franco Baresi, a legendary defender for AC Milan and the Italian national team, has died at the age of 66. Baresi was celebrated for his contributions to football during the 1980s and 1990s, including winning the World Cup with Italy.

explore_lenses.label: What made Baresi central to AC Milan?
explore_lenses.title: A one-club captain of Milan’s dominant era
explore_lenses.summary: Baresi’s legacy rests on both longevity and leadership: he spent his entire senior playing career at Milan and captained sides that became European powers in the late 1980s and early 1990s. The club’s record and FIFA’s retrospective also show why he is associated with the evolution of the libero role.

claims.text: AC Milan records 719 official appearances for Baresi, along with six Serie A titles, three European Cups, two Intercontinental Cups and four Italian Supercups.
FIFA describes Baresi as a sweeper who helped revolutionize the position, combining defensive work with leadership and counterattacking distribution.
AC Milan says he remained with the club through difficult years, including relegation, before captaining teams coached by Arrigo Sacchi and Fabio Capello during their period of international success.
AC Milan framed his Hall of Fame induction as recognition not only of his achievements but also of his conduct and long-term commitment to the club.

explore_lenses.label: How did his World Cup career unfold?
explore_lenses.title: A 1982 winner and 1994 finalist
explore_lenses.summary: Baresi’s World Cup record spans Italy’s 1982 title and its defeat in the 1994 final. The 1982 winner’s medal is an important nuance: FIFA says he did not play in that tournament, whereas he captained Italy in the 1994 final after a rapid recovery from knee surgery.

claims.text: Italy won the 1982 World Cup, and Baresi was part of the squad; FIFA says he received a winner’s medal but did not play at the tournament.
Baresi made 81 appearances for Italy between 1982 and 1994, according to FIFA.
He captained Italy in the 1994 World Cup final against Brazil, which finished 0-0 before Brazil won the penalty shootout 3-2.
FIFA reports that Baresi returned to play all 120 minutes of the 1994 final only 22 days after knee surgery, after being injured in Italy’s second group match.

story_report.summary: Franco Baresi, the former AC Milan and Italy defender who was a leading figure in Italian football during the 1980s and 1990s, has died aged 66. The Italian Football Federation’s president, Giovanni Malagò, said Italy would pay tribute to Baresi when the national team next plays. No date has been announced for that tribute, and the consulted material did not identify plans for a funeral or stadium ceremony.

sections.heading: Franco Baresi’s AC Milan Legacy
sections.body: Baresi made 719 official appearances for AC Milan, winning six Serie A titles, three European Cups, two Intercontinental Cups and four Italian Supercups, according to the club. Milan says he stayed through difficult years that included relegation before captaining successful sides coached by Arrigo Sacchi and Fabio Capello. The club retired his No. 6 shirt after his 1997 retirement, named him Honorary Vice-President in 2020 and made him its first official Hall of Fame inductee in 2024.

sections.heading: Franco Baresi’s Italy Career
sections.body: Baresi made 81 appearances for Italy between 1982 and 1994. He was in Italy’s 1982 World Cup-winning squad and received a winner’s medal, though he did not play in the tournament. At the 1994 World Cup, he captained Italy in the final against Brazil, returning from knee surgery to play all 120 minutes only 22 days after the operation; the match ended 0-0 before Brazil won the shootout 3-2. FIFA describes him as a sweeper who combined defending, leadership and counterattacking distribution.

related_stories.title: FIFA President Infantino Faces Pressure After Senior Advisor Resigns Over Investment Plans
related_stories.summary: Carlos Cordeiro, a senior advisor to FIFA President Gianni Infantino, has resigned amid growing backlash against Infantino's proposal for private investment in the World Cup. The resignation follows condemnation from regional football federations, including North America and Europe, which have rejected the investment plan. Critics argue that selling stakes in the World Cup could harm the integrity of football.

related_stories.title: UEFA Threatens Boycott of FIFA Tournaments Over World Cup Investment Plans
related_stories.summary: UEFA has voted to boycott FIFA tournaments, including the World Cup, in response to FIFA's plans to allow private investors to buy stakes in a potential commercial subsidiary. UEFA argues that the tournament should not be treated as an investment product. Despite this opposition, FIFA remains committed to pursuing its investment strategy and has offered financial incentives to countries that support the initiative.

related_stories.title: UEFA Threatens Boycott of World Cups Over FIFA's Investor Plan
related_stories.summary: UEFA has declared its intent to boycott future FIFA World Cups if FIFA President Gianni Infantino's proposal to allow private investors to control the tournament's commercial rights is implemented. During an emergency meeting, all 55 member associations of UEFA voted unanimously in favor of this stance, emphasizing that 'the World Cup is not for sale.'

related_stories.title: Trump Indicates No Objection to Withdrawing Todd Blanche's Nomination Amid Senate Delays
related_stories.summary: President Donald Trump has stated he has 'no objection' to withdrawing Todd Blanche's nomination for Attorney General. This comes as two Republican senators, Thom Tillis and John Cornyn, are withholding support, leading to a delay in the Senate vote. The senators are seeking a written commitment from the Department of Justice regarding a disputed compensation fund that could benefit Trump allies.
